summary: Customer reported a recent multi-region latency variance and a one-off cascade where fallback policies didn't trigger cleanly. This call focused on the "latency entropy" concept (distributional jitter across routing paths) and how Redwood's fallthroughs, KV/prefix caching and quantization profiles interact in staging vs dedicated deployments. Agreed immediate steps: share security artifacts, run a controlled benchmark with Redwood's harness, and a pilot to validate fallthrough policy + cache priming. SE dug into traces and proposed changes to sampling windows, cache TTLs, and a conservative canary rollback policy.
topics: fallthrough policies and model variant routing
KV cache priming and prefix caching behavior
dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for deterministic latency
benchmark plan and pilot next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, appreciate it. we wanted to do a deep dive into the jitter you saw last week and then map that to a mitigation plan. long agenda short — figure out whether this is routing entropy versus cache coldness.
[00:18] Maya (Paladin): thanks Sofia. yeah we had two customer-facing errors where latency spiked to 3.2s p95 from our typical 420ms, and on one path the fallback to the smaller model didn't happen, the UI timed out. log traces attached in the ticket.
[00:36] Liam (SRE): and to add we saw KV cache miss rates spike around 03:12 UTC, which looks correlated. but the routing metrics show occasional cross-region hops; we suspect a transient p95 tail from the cloud balancer.
[00:50] Ethan (Redwood SE): okay, quick note — sometimes the LB reorders affinity and that interacts poorly with cold KV caches. the runtime keeps a KV cache per-alloc, if a request jumps allocs the prefix isn't available, so you get a cold-start penalty plus any model conversion time if it had to go to a quantized variant.
[01:10] Priya (Security): one quick reminder from our side: any pilot will need to validate KMS integration and audit log continuity, we can't have keys exported or gaps in immutable logs.
[01:24] Sofia: totally, priya, we'll include the SOC2 artifacts and a KMS/HSM note. also onboarding can be VPC or dedicated — we should map the deterministic latency needs to dedicated pools.
[01:40] Carlos (Backend Lead): just to be explicit: we prefer dedicated GPUs if the unit economics work, but we need to prove the latency delta is material for our flows. we saw one user journey where we have 12 tokens prefixed then a 1.2k context body, so sequence lengths are big.
[02:02] Ethan: thanks Carlos, that's helpful. big context plus frequent allocation hops is exactly the pathological case. two levers: make cache priming aggressive (longer prefix TTL, proactive KV write on warm warm paths) and tighten routing affinity so the same alloc serves the session. also look at batch windows — longer windows reduce unit cost but increase latency variance.
[02:28] Liam: can you explain the fallthrough mismatch? why didn't it switch to the cheaper model?
[02:35] Ethan: short answer: a race. the fallback policy is policy-first but needs a consistent signal from the orchestrator. if the orchestrator thinks capacity exists and the node later reports overload, the runtime may attempt an on-node fallback that doesn't have the model cached. we saw in the traces an on-the-fly model load that missed the SLO deadline. that's an edge-case.
[02:58] Sofia: so for mitigation today we have three parts: 1) avoid the race by pre-warming fallback model variants on canary nodes, 2) use a conservative fallback timeout that triggers remote routing earlier, 3) add a short-circuit so the API returns an explicit fallback decision fast and we can instrument it.
[03:22] Maya: pre-warming sounds good, but that increases memory and cost — how do we quantify it?
[03:28] Ethan: yep, tradeoff. we'll produce a small cost model: pre-warm X GB per alloc vs the outage minutes saved. Redwood Optimize suggestions can generate a delta. I'll provide numbers from our benchmark harness.
[03:40] Priya: on the audit side, if you pre-warm models do you leak model telemetry into customer logs? we need to ensure no PII is included and that KV cache keys are hashed and not customer strings.
[03:50] Ethan: by design we hash prefix keys client-side and the runtime stores opaque caches. still we will document the guarantee and show a sanitized trace.
[04:02] Nora (CSM): note: I'll share a checklist for pilot gating criteria (SLO targets, rollback steps, contact list).
[04:12] Carlos: quick question — we use an in-house proxy that terminates TLS then forwards groups of requests; could that be altering affinity and causing the alloc hop?
[04:21] Ethan: yes that can. if the proxy opens multiple backend connections and round-robins, you lose session-level affinity. recommend either sticky backend connections or include a session affinity header to the Redwood routing layer.
[04:38] Liam: for the benchmark harness, what do you need from us?
[04:42] Ethan: two flows: 1) short-chat (avg 40 tokens, p95 ~ 100 tokens), 2) long-context (1.2k TL, mixed prompt + system). also a token length distribution CSV, and any proxy config we can replicate. with that we run with: hosted config, dedicated config (same hardware), and a dedicated-with-prewarm config.
[05:08] Maya: okay we'll get the flows and distribution. another thing: we saw a small memory leak after repeated model loads in the hot path last month — is that a known risk with the quantized loader?
[05:18] Ethan: we have an open patch that reduces loader GC pressure but it hasn't shipped to prod. it is part of the 0.9.4 runtime release. for the pilot we'll use the patched runtime on dedicated nodes.
[05:29] Priya: security checklist items — SAML SSO behavior, KMS key rotation policy, retention windows for raw request payloads, and audit log retention. we'll need a statement about on-prem HSM compatibility.
[05:44] Sofia: we'll produce a one-pager and a short FAQ for HSM integrations. link to internal security pack (redacted) is in the notes, we'll send the customer-facing version.
[05:55] Maya: can you walk through what the fallthrough decision path looks like in logs? i.e. how do we detect it in our traces?
[06:02] Ethan: sure — you'll see three markers: route_decision, model_load_start, model_load_complete or fallback_trigger. route_decision shows intended target; if model_load_start happens and model_load_complete is absent before the SLO, you'll see a fallback_trigger event. we'll annotate the example traces.
[06:20] Carlos: would lambda-style cold starts be a better metaphor?
[06:24] Ethan: kind of, yes. but the runtime supports prefix caching and KV snapshots to reduce cold start cost — treat pre-warm like a warm lambda layer pinned to nodes.
[06:34] Liam: curious about the quantization profiles you mentioned — you said some conversions add 40ms?
[06:38] Ethan: depends on the model and kernel selection; converting to a int8 runtime path can add 20-120ms per first load due to kernel warmups. subsequent inferences are faster and cheaper. hence pre-warm is useful.
[06:52] Priya: any compliance risk from using quantized variants? we need to ensure deterministic outputs for audit-critical flows.
[06:58] Ethan: quantization can change numeric determinism slightly; for audit-critical responses you should pin a float32 variant or set deterministic sampling flags, even if cost is higher. we recommend that for high-assurance decisions.
[07:12] Sofia: quick demo plan: we'll run an A/B across canary nodes with 1% traffic, compare route entropy and miss rate, then step to 10% if metrics look good. rollback is automatic with a 5-min guard window.
[07:26] Maya: i want to be able to trigger a manual rollback from our console if needed.
[07:30] Nora: yes we'll add you as a pilot admin for the rollback button and we'll walk through the runbook.
[07:38] Carlos: about the proxy affinity header — is that something we add or Redwood adds a header consumers can pass?
[07:44] Ethan: either. we accept an x-redwood-session header that seeds routing. if your proxy can attach it per session then affinity is preserved. otherwise we can negotiate sticky connections.
[07:56] Liam: on observability, can we get token-level breakdowns so we can see which parts of the prompt cost the most latency?
[08:02] Ethan: yes, Redwood Console can show per-token time across stages (decode, kv-lookup, kernel). we'll grant you access to a sandbox dashboard for the pilot.
[08:12] Priya: also need to confirm that transcript storage for debugging can be redacted or disabled in pilot — we're okay with telemetry but not customer text retention beyond 7 days without explicit legal sign-off.
[08:24] Sofia: understood, we'll provide a retention toggle and show the sanitized audit logs.
[08:30] Maya: timeline question: how long until we can run the pilot? we want to minimize user impact and run during low traffic window.
[08:36] Sofia: if you can share the flows + proxy config by Monday 11/09, we can prepare a patched runtime image and benchmark harness by 11/12, then a pilot the week of 11/15 depending on your ops availability.
[08:51] Ethan: i'll also jot down the config flags we plan to toggle: prewarm=true, fallback_timeout=300ms, session_affinity=header, cache_ttl=60m (default staging candidate).
[09:02] Carlos: cache_ttl 60m sounds long — can we start with 15m? we worry about memory.
[09:07] Ethan: yep start conservative, maybe 15m for staging, 60m for dedicated pre-warm. we'll measure hit rates.
[09:14] Liam: will you share the harness script and the expected output format so our SRE can run it locally?
[09:20] Ethan: yes, harness is a small Python tool that emulates the session flows. we'll attach it to the ticket with instructions.
[09:28] Priya: last thing from security — we need an SLA exception clause for pilot to cover temporary logging changes and we need clear contact paths if we detect PII leaks.
[09:38] Sofia: we'll draft an annex for the pilot that enumerates temporary telemetry options and contact escalation steps.
[09:45] Nora: recap: Redwood shares security docs and KMS FAQ; SE provides harness and pre-warm cost model; Paladin provides flows, proxy config, and network diagram; schedule pilot week of 11/15. action items in the channel.
[09:58] Maya: thanks all. can we get a short recording and the notes?
[10:02] Nora: yes i'll push the recording and a concise notes doc to the ticket, and i'll add the pilot gating checklist.
[10:10] Sofia: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the SOC2 + KMS doc and a proposed pilot runbook.
[10:16] Carlos: thanks. bye.
[10:18] End of recording.
